audit_findings.title: Consolidated owner earnings may not belong entirely to common shareholders
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated depreciation, capital expenditure, working-capital movements, and disposal proceeds may inflate common-shareholder OE if they were combined with parent-attributable earnings without allocating NCI portions.
audit_findings.evidence: Net earnings attributable to noncontrolling interest primarily represents our joint venture partner's share in the results of operations of our Mexican railcar manufacturing joint ventures, adjusted for intercompany sales, and our European partner’s share of the results of our European operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that consolidated operations include ordinary and redeemable NCI, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether each OE component was consistently allocated. The possible error is material: 2025 NCI earnings were $9.0 million, while a recurring $7.9 million reduction in the $111.3 million anchor would eliminate the approximately $111.4 million base-value premium over market value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year using parent-attributable cash-flow components, separately allocating D&A, capex, working capital, asset-sale proceeds, taxes, and distributions to ordinary and redeemable NCI; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The Astra put may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.9 million recorded carrying amount, equal to approximately $0.80 per valuation share; ultimate cash obligation unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any parent-funded redemption payment is a senior bridge deduction from equity value unless already captured in OE or another liability adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: Astra received a put option to sell its entire noncontrolling interest to the Company at an exercise price equal to the higher of fair value or a defined earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) multiple as measured on the exercise date.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission of the recorded $31.9 million mezzanine interest is demonstrated and would reduce base value from $46.06 to approximately $45.26 per share, which alone would not reverse the base comparison with the $43.26 price. However, the put price is the higher of fair value or a defined EBITDA multiple, and the May 2026 filing says that price remains undetermined. The record therefore cannot establish whether the ultimate claim is large enough to change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the written put-price determination, valuation calculation, exercise status, settlement terms, funding source, and any post-filing remeasurement; deduct the parent-funded amount and rerun the bridge and margin-of-safety price.

audit_findings.title: Lease-fleet replacement capital may be understated
audit_findings.mechanism: Understated recurring fleet maintenance, refurbishment, and replacement capital overstates sustainable OE and every forecast-period and terminal cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: The rent we receive during the initial railcar lease term typically covers only a small portion of the railcar acquisition or production costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a capital-intensive fleet but does not demonstrate how much fleet spending is maintenance rather than expansion. The scale is capable of changing the conclusion: 2025 Leasing & Fleet Management capex was $140.5 million versus $43.1 million of segment D&A, and only about $7.9 million of recurring anchor-OE reduction would erase the base-value premium over the market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile fleet units, age, utilization, lease revenue, refurbishments, retirements, acquisitions, depreciation, disposal proceeds, and gains by year; estimate capital required to preserve fleet economics and rerun OE and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include required operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: $273.7 million added; operationally required portion unquantified; $111.4 million, or 40.7% of the add-back, would eliminate the base-value premium
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash that is restricted, trapped, committed, or required for operations must be excluded from the equity bridge rather than added as distributable surplus.
audit_findings.evidence: Our current cash balance is part of our strategy to maintain strong liquidity to respond to current uncertainties.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds all $273.7 million of cash and cash equivalents, while the filing describes the balance as part of the liquidity strategy. The unavailable portion is not established, but it need only exceed approximately $111.4 million to reduce base value to the current market capitalization, so this is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a legal-entity cash schedule identifying parent-accessible, JV, subsidiary, covenant-restricted, pledged, and operational cash; establish minimum liquidity through a working-capital and covenant stress test, then rerun the bridge using only excess distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: The convertible-share ceiling mismatches after-interest owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 8.1 million excess reserved shares; removing them reduces the denominator from 39.889686 million to 31.789686 million and produces approximately $45.86 bear, $57.79 base, and $66.66 bull value per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The mechanically added reserved shares dilute per-share value even though principal is cash-settled and after-interest OE already bears the note interest; only an economically issuable conversion premium belongs in shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Conversion of the par value of the note will be settled in cash, with any premium convertible in cash or shares at the Company’s option.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator error. The filing states that principal must be settled in cash, only the premium may be share-settled, and the notes had no dilutive effect when the stock price was below the conversion price. Removing only the 8.1 million reserved-share ceiling materially increases every per-share scenario and changes the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun using after-interest OE and only premium shares issuable under the indenture at each scenario value; separately model any cash required for principal settlement without mechanically issuing the reserved-share ceiling.

audit_findings.title: An unquantified environmental claim is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probable parent-funded remediation, natural-resource-damages, or settlement payment not captured in recurring OE is a senior deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Because these environmental investigations are still underway, sufficient information is currently not available to determine the Company’s liability, if any, for the cost of any required remediation or restoration of the Portland Harbor Superfund Site or to estimate a range of potential loss.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure is real, but no company-specific liability or estimable range is supplied. The filed $1.7 billion estimate covers the entire Superfund remedy and cannot be assigned to Greenbrier, while historical company expenditures were described as not material. The record therefore supports neither a zero adjustment nor a finding that the exposure can change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain allocation-process estimates, RM9W cost information, confidential settlement demands where available, insurance and indemnity coverage, contribution claims, legal-probability assessments, and post-filing developments; rerun the bridge for any supportable parent-funded exposure scenarios.
